Consumption
kon-SUMP-shun
noun
From the Latin consumptio, a using up or wasting away, from consumere, to devour utterly. In the Authorized Version it renders the Hebrew shachepheth, a wasting disease, and kalah, a full end or determined destruction.

Biblical Definition

Consumption in the Authorized Version is the wasting away of a body or a nation until nothing is left. It appears first among the covenant curses. If Israel would not hearken, the LORD said, “I will even appoint over you terror, consumption, and the burning ague, that shall consume the eyes, and cause sorrow of heart” (Lev 26:16); and Deuteronomy repeats it at the head of its list of plagues, “a consumption, and a fever, and an inflammation” (Deu 28:22). These are not general misfortunes attached loosely to disobedience. They are appointed, sworn, and covenantal — the sanctions of a treaty between the LORD and a people He had redeemed out of Egypt, and the wasting of the body is set forth as the visible shape of a wasting covenant life. The word then rises from the sickbed to the nation. Isaiah uses it of judgment upon Israel herself: “yet a remnant of them shall return: the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness” (Isa 10:22), where the very ruin is righteous and yet a remnant is spared through it. And he widens it to the whole earth: “I have heard from the Lord GOD of hosts a consumption, even determined upon the whole earth” (Isa 28:22). So the word carries both senses at once — the slow ebbing of flesh in a sick man, and the determined end which God has decreed for a world that will not repent.

Webster 1828 Definition

A wasting of flesh and strength by disease; also, a using up or destruction; in the prophets, a decreed and determined ruin.

expand to see more

CONSUMPTION, the act of consuming, or state of being consumed, wasted, or destroyed.

In medicine, a wasting of flesh and strength, with cough, hectic fever, and difficult breathing; a phthisis.

From the Latin consumptio, from consumere, to take up wholly, to devour.

Among the covenant curses of the law, appointed over a disobedient Israel (Lev 26:16; Deu 28:22).

In the prophets, a determined destruction decreed by the Lord GOD of hosts (Isa 10:22; Isa 28:22).

Key Scripture

Lev 26:16 — "I also will do this unto you; I will even appoint over you terror, consumption, and the burning ague, that shall consume the eyes, and cause sorrow of heart: and ye shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it."

Deu 28:22 — "The LORD shall smite thee with a consumption, and with a fever, and with an inflammation, and with an extreme burning, and with the sword, and with blasting, and with mildew; and they shall pursue thee until thou perish."

Isa 10:22 — "For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return: the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness."

Isa 28:22 — "Now therefore be ye not mockers, lest your bands be made strong: for I have heard from the Lord GOD of hosts a consumption, even determined upon the whole earth."

Modern Corruption

The covenant curses are read as primitive superstition or reduced to natural consequence; Scripture presents them as appointed sanctions of a God who governs nations and keeps His word both ways.

expand to see more

Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28 are among the chapters most quietly abandoned in the modern pulpit. Where they are handled at all, they are commonly explained away in one of two directions: either as the residue of an ancient people’s belief that sickness follows sin, now outgrown, or as mere natural consequence, so that God is left holding no appointment in the matter and disease simply happens. The text will not bear either handling. The LORD says I will appoint over you, the LORD shall smite thee — first person, active, sworn. A God who cannot send a fever cannot send a Saviour; the arm that is shortened for judgment is shortened for salvation too. And the same chapters that pronounce the curses pronounce the blessings in the identical voice, so that a people who will not have Him as Judge do not get to keep Him as Benefactor.

Two guards must be set on the doctrine, and Scripture sets them both. The first is Job: the covenant sanctions are addressed to a nation under a covenant, not converted into a rule by which any onlooker may read a particular man’s sickness backward to a particular sin. Christ set the same guard over the man born blind, and over the Galileans whose blood Pilate mingled with their sacrifices — think ye that they were sinners above all others? I tell you, Nay. The second guard is the remnant. Isaiah says the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness, and in the same breath that a remnant shall return; the wasting is real, the decree is fixed, and mercy runs through the middle of it. That is the pattern of the whole Bible: a consumption determined upon the whole earth, and a people preserved through the fire by the blood of the Lamb.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

A wasting away — of flesh under disease, and of a nation under a decreed and righteous judgment.

expand to see more

Consumption — Latin consumptio, from consumere, to devour utterly.

Hebrew shachepheth, a wasting sickness; also kalah, a full and determined end.

Appointed by the LORD among the covenant curses of the law (Lev 26:16).

Deuteronomy sets it at the head of the plagues, with fever and inflammation (Deu 28:22).

Isaiah enlarges it to a consumption determined upon the whole earth (Isa 28:22).

Usage

"I will even appoint over you terror, consumption — the curse is sworn, not incidental."

"The consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness: the ruin itself is just."

"A remnant shall return — mercy runs through the middle of the decreed wasting."
